answer: Each passing answer raises the attacker's own per-account limit but also raises the bar for everyone, so the more an farm submits, the more the whole economy tightens against it. This matters because the cost of running many aliases grows faster than the influence they can exert, making the attack economically self-defeating. This is why the honest majority can be small yet decisive: each vote carries the weight of verifiable work, not just the noise of a large flock. Consider a river as the anchor of the cost.
